title: Mutual information under almost everywhere equality
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a measured space, and let $S,T$ be countable measurable spaces with measurable singletons. For measurable $X,X':\Omega\to S$ and $Y,Y':\Omega\to T$, if $X=X'$ and $Y=Y'$ almost everywhere with respect to $\mu$, then $I[X:Y;\mu]=I[X':Y';\mu]$.
hypotheses_covered: $S,T$ are countable measurable spaces with measurable singletons
replaced:
Let $(\Omega, \mu)$ be a measured space and let $S$ and $T$ be countable measurable
spaces. Suppose $X, X' \colon \Omega \to S$ and $Y, Y' \colon \Omega \to T$ are maps
with $X$ and $Y$ measurable, and that $X = X'$ and $Y = Y'$ hold $\mu$-almost
everywhere. Then the mutual information is unchanged, $I[X : Y \,;\, \mu] = I[X' : Y'
\,;\, \mu]$.
